questions.q: What is the defining characteristic of circuit switching that distinguishes it from packet switching?
questions.a: Circuit switching establishes a dedicated physical path (or logical channel) between endpoints for the entire session duration, reserving bandwidth continuously. A wrong answer like "data is divided into packets" reveals confusion with packet switching. A wrong answer like "it uses store-and-forward" reveals confusion with message switching. The student must recall the reservation concept, not just any feature.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why packet switching is more efficient than circuit switching for bursty data traffic like web browsing.
questions.a: Packet switching allows multiple users to share the same link by statistically multiplexing packets; when one user is idle (reading a page), others can use the bandwidth. Circuit switching would reserve bandwidth even during idle think-time, wasting capacity. A wrong answer focusing only on "packets are smaller" or "packets take different routes" misses the core concept of statistical multiplexing and shared resource utilization during silence periods.

questions.q: A company needs to connect two offices for a continuous 8-hour daily video conference requiring 2 Mbps constant bitrate. The available link is 10 Mbps shared with other bursty traffic. Which switching technique should they choose and why? Provide two technical reasons.
questions.a: Choose circuit switching (or a dedicated leased line / virtual circuit with guaranteed bandwidth). Reasons: (1) Video conference requires constant bitrate and low, predictable jitter — circuit switching reserves 2 Mbps continuously, guaranteeing quality. (2) With 8-hour daily usage, the reservation duty cycle is high (33%), making reservation efficient; packet switching would risk variable delay and packet loss during congestion from other bursty traffic. A wrong answer choosing packet switching because "it's modern" ignores the QoS requirements of constant-bitrate real-time traffic.

questions.q: Compare circuit switching and packet switching on the following dimensions: (a) connection setup delay, (b) per-packet/per-bit delay during transfer, (c) robustness to link failure. Present as a table.
questions.a:
| Dimension | Circuit Switching | Packet Switching |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Setup delay | High (path reservation before data) | Low/N/A (datagram) or moderate (virtual circuit) |
| (b) Transfer delay | Constant, low (no queuing once reserved) | Variable (queuing, routing per packet) |
| (c) Robustness | Low (path break tears down session) | High (packets reroute around failure) |
A wrong answer that swaps (b) or claims packet switching has constant delay reveals misunderstanding of queuing in shared links. A wrong answer claiming circuit switching is robust reveals ignorance of single-path dependency.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "Packet switching is always superior to circuit switching because it uses bandwidth more efficiently." Defend or refute with two specific counter-examples where circuit switching is preferable.
questions.a: Refute. Counter-example 1: Traditional PSTN voice calls — circuit switching provides guaranteed 64 kbps with negligible jitter, essential for real-time conversation; packet switching (VoIP) requires complex QoS to match. Counter-example 2: High-frequency trading links — microsecond-level deterministic latency is critical; circuit-switched (or dedicated fiber) eliminates queuing uncertainty. A wrong answer agreeing with the statement shows inability to evaluate trade-offs; a wrong counter-example like "file transfer" actually favors packet switching.

questions.q: Design a hybrid network scenario for a smart factory where both circuit-switched and packet-switched segments coexist. Describe the traffic types assigned to each and the interconnection point.
questions.a: Example: Factory floor sensors (temperature, pressure) send periodic small bursts → packet-switched Ethernet to local gateway. Robotic arm control loops require 1 ms cycle time with zero jitter → circuit-switched (or time-sensitive networking TSN) dedicated fibers to motion controller. Interconnection: Gateway router with TSN-capable ports bridges packet domain to circuit domain, using priority queuing to give control traffic precedence. A poor answer assigns all traffic to one technique or fails to specify the bridging mechanism, showing lack of synthesis.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Circuit switching establishes a dedicated end-to-end physical path between sender and receiver for the entire ______ session, reserving bandwidth regardless of usage.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are on a phone call (circuit switched) versus sending a ______ message (packet switched).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can (1) explain the fundamental operational difference between circuit and packet switching using the concepts of resource reservation vs. statistical multiplexing, and (2) given a communication scenario (e.g., live video call vs. email), justify which switching technique is more appropriate with at least two technical.
